old_problem: Items requires H.264 encoding, while Procedure contains no encode step and only asks to display video and inspect undefined visual issues/`bleeding edge`; Criteria is TBD. These are different NVENC, decode and scanout pipelines. DeepSeek's CPU libx264-to-null example exercises none of the claimed GPU encode identity, retained bitstream, reverse decode or physical pixels, while GPT V2's combined pipeline is a plausible future design but not an approved resolution of which source layer is authoritative.
disposition_reason: Retain Engineering Decision Pending, Source Conflict and BLOCKED after official research. NVIDIA documents NVENC hardware encoding and NVDEC hardware decoding as distinct engines, and FFmpeg separately defines CPU `libx264` and GPU `h264_nvenc`; a valid result in one cannot prove the others or physical scanout. Public specifications can define safe commands after scope is chosen, but they cannot decide whether this private row's title or Procedure is authoritative, nor define `bleeding edge` or a numeric/golden visual oracle. This is missing core operation and PASS/FAIL authority, not merely runtime GPU/profile values. A parameterized stage ledger is provided so the case can be completed promptly once the owner rules encode-only, decode/display-only, or separately accepted combined checkpoints.
decision_basis: The exact XLSX row 1780, same-row DeepSeek/test-json content, GPT V2, historical V3.1 conflict/blocked record, original pending/conflict/blocked analyses, exact-code search, adjacent H.265 row and ED rules were read. The actual next formal queue identity was directly opened as Functionality row 1781 / Wistron-HW-00414-V002 / 994b8e5daeb3a934.

NVIDIA NVENC produces an H.264-compliant bitstream from input frames; NVIDIA NVDEC independently decodes H.264 into frames that may later be displayed. Encoder success therefore does not prove decoder or physical-display behavior, and playback of a known file does not test encode.

FFmpeg documents `libx264` as the software x264 wrapper and `h264_nvenc` as the NVIDIA hardware encoder whose features depend on build headers, GPU and driver. DeepSeek's `-c:v libx264 -f null -` cannot establish NVENC use and leaves no output for the claimed reverse decode.

Combining encode, decode and display would preserve both textual cues but would add a pipeline relationship and acceptance model absent from Master. It cannot be called RESOLVED until Engineering explicitly approves separate checkpoints or selects one authoritative stage.

The phrase `bleeding edge` has no deterministic codec/display meaning in this context. A visual reference/golden frames and allowed artifact/tolerance, or an owner-defined direct visual checklist, are required; no threshold may be invented under ED-18/ED-30 principles.
The following H.265 Source Key is a distinct codec identity under ED-21 and cannot resolve or absorb H.264 scope, even though the wording is similar.
No ffmpeg, NVENC, NVDEC, playback, visual inspection, scratch write, log clear or other DUT action was executed.
